explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a garden vegetable grown for its peppery root, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Performance is popular, in a way

indicators.note: the word in signals one piece sitting inside the other

parts.note: a route is a way from one place to another
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A show proves a hit, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian's or dancer's set piece, the act they perform, is called their routine.

clue.text: Club in which the password is courage

indicators.note: the answer sits in which the following words run, inside the phrase about the password

explanation.surface: A members' club whose secret password is the word courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'password is courage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub where people dance to recorded music is a type of club.

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or faulty, so the letters are unsound and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A shock unsettles someone called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' poses as a man's name but is the anagram signal, rearranging RATTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock, a verb synonym of surprise.

clue.text: Old Bob impresses designs on seats

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s
to tool leather or a book cover is to press decorative patterns into it

explanation.surface: A man named Bob, getting on, decorates chairs with patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 Britain's shilling was nicknamed a bob and written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stools are backless seats for one person, so they are examples of seats.

parts.note: to taunt is to mock or ridicule
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Mockery is at work in the English county of Somerset.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is the county town of Somerset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition reads as a place located in that county, which the town is.

clue.text: Respond immoderately and veto racer after crashing

indicators.note: crashing smashes the words up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and bans a racing driver after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges VETO RACER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to show a stronger response than a situation warrants.

parts.note: a committee or court sits when it meets in session
someone doing well is flourishing

explanation.surface: An encounter with a thriving versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was an English poet of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell, the English modernist versifier, is an example of a poet.

indicators.note: we hear says the word for candid is spoken, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: frank means candid or outspoken

explanation.surface: A musician is said to be outspoken.
explanation.walkthrough: César Franck was a Belgian-French composer of the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: César Franck wrote a famous symphony and violin sonata, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Rules out nastier play in dangerous game

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are moved about freely, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rule forbids nasty play in a risky game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges RULES OUT NASTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: The game of firing a revolver with one loaded chamber at one's own head is deadly risky.

indicators.note: after puts the solicitor piece following the welcome piece

parts.note: hi is a word of welcome
a tout solicits custom, so is one who solicits

explanation.surface: A lawyer gets a dressing-down after being greeted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer but means a tout, someone touting for business.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit out at someone is to attack them verbally, to criticise them harshly.

parts.note: not stands for never, a flat negative
Aries is one of the twelve houses of the zodiac in astrology

explanation.surface: An instruction never to give officials a home.
explanation.walkthrough: In astrology the signs of the zodiac are called houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are public officers who certify documents, so they are officials.

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
a break is a pause or suspension of activity

explanation.surface: Support for a suspension of a postal delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg break is a ball spun by the bowler; a bowled ball is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket each ball bowled is a delivery, and a spinning ball turning from the leg side is one type.

clue.text: Gambler out to become more wealthy

parts.note: one who bets is a better, a gambler
a light that is off is out

explanation.surface: A punter sets out to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Being better off means having more money, an idiom for being richer.

indicators.note: capital means the capital, or first, letter of the word Namibian

parts.note: something at an early stage is not yet developed

explanation.surface: Is Windhoek, Namibia's capital, barely developed? Almost so!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Namibian capital' suggests Windhoek but means only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and just about both mean almost, an adverbial synonym.

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a road
to long or yearn for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: Mending a road takes a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective about the road, but it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch a tear is to sew it up, a way of repairing cloth.

clue.text: Taught delinquent once about bad weather

parts.note: a Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British youth thought of as a delinquent
rain is unwelcome, bad weather

explanation.surface: A former young offender was taught about storms.
explanation.walkthrough: Teds were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style clothes, seen as hooligans.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained and taught both describe someone who has been instructed in a skill.

parts.note: hands are helpers
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: Assistance for one's child that means joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: Hands as help is the plural workers sense, extra hands to assist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on approach means doing the work oneself rather than directing from afar.

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician was knocked down for dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LAID into DILA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory means slow and causing delay, describing a time-wasting person or manner.

parts.note: de is the French word for of
to ride is to travel

explanation.surface: Contempt for French travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock with contempt, a verb synonym of scorn.

indicators.note: representation suggests a rendering of the letters in another form, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A version of a document in Braille for an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' rearranges BRAILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal is a member of a Liberal party, so a type of politician.

clue.text: Teacher served up only item on the menu

sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the teacher's title backwards; British pupils call a male teacher sir.

clue.text: Old publican and sailor entertaining French writer

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
Jules Verne was a French novelist

explanation.surface: An innkeeper and a seaman host a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverner is an archaic word for one who keeps a tavern, an innkeeper.

clue.text: Throw out Northern Ireland leaders found in party

indicators.note: found in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the words Northern and Ireland

explanation.surface: Politicians from Northern Ireland are expelled from a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the initials of Northern Ireland, and 'found in' sets them inside the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel or send them away, to throw them out.

clue.text: Letter on top of desk is prominent

parts.note: a note is a short letter

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of desk, in a down clue the topmost

explanation.surface: A letter lying on a desk stands out.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or eminent, so prominent in a field.

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb to act but is the swindle sense; 'in' sets it within the word for private.

clue.text: River without end in Paris? Explain!

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here has its old sense of outside, so the river encloses the French word, not loses a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To define something is to state its meaning precisely, a way to explain it.
